doc.section: APIs and Interfaces - Frontend API Client Pattern

doc.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification - Simple Answer Experience
doc.section: Workflows and Sequencing - Primary User Flow
doc.snippet: User submits location → page.tsx sets isLoading=true → POST /api/check-rain with {location} → Backend processes (Epic 2 logic) → API responds with YES/NO answer → page.tsx updates state (answerData or errorData) → AnswerDisplay or ErrorDisplay renders result. Complete flow must work end-to-end with proper state management and error handling.

doc.title: Epic 2 Technical Specification - Weather Intelligence Engine
doc.snippet: Backend API route at app/api/check-rain/route.ts. Request: {location: string}. Success response includes willRain boolean, probability number, rainWindows array, peakTime string, intensity string, amount string, safeWindows array, closeCall boolean. HTTP status codes: 200 (success), 400 (invalid request), 404 (location not found), 500 (server error), 504 (timeout). Error response: {error: ErrorCode, message: string, suggestions?: string[]}

doc.title: Architecture - Project Structure
doc.section: Integration Points - Frontend to Backend API
doc.snippet: Frontend communicates with backend via POST /api/check-rain. API endpoint is on same domain (no CORS needed). All API calls use relative path. Request includes Content-Type: application/json header. Backend processes using OpenWeather API and returns formatted response. Frontend parses response and updates state for display.

doc.title: Architecture - Implementation Patterns
doc.snippet: Backend implements retry logic for 5xx errors (single retry, 5-second timeout). Frontend must handle all error types: invalid_location, service_unavailable, timeout, network_error. All fetch calls wrapped in try-catch. Network errors caught and mapped to user-friendly messages. No dead ends - user can always retry.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document - TEST3
doc.section: Functional Requirements - FR3.4 Search Again Functionality
doc.snippet: Input field remains accessible after answer displayed. User can search new location without page reload. Previous results cleared when new search initiated. State properly reset between searches. No navigation required to search again.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document - TEST3
doc.snippet: Total time from search submission to answer display must be under 2 seconds. Backend timeout at 5 seconds. Frontend should display loading state immediately (under 100ms). Single API call per search action. No redundant network calls.

node.purpose: App Router framework, provides fetch API client-side
useState for state management, useRef for focus management
Type safety for API contracts, strict mode enabled

constraints.constraint: Use native Fetch API only - no axios or HTTP libraries (ADR-005). API calls use relative path /api/check-rain on same domain.
API client must use POST method with Content-Type: application/json header. Request body must be JSON.stringify({location: string}).
All error handling must wrap fetch in try-catch. Network errors map to network_error type with message: "Network connection failed. Please check your internet and try again."
Backend has 5-second timeout. Frontend should handle timeout gracefully (backend returns 504 status with timeout error).
State management: answerData and errorData are mutually exclusive. Clear both before new API call. Set isLoading=true before call, false after response.
TypeScript strict mode - no any types allowed. All API responses must be typed as RainCheckResponse | ErrorResponse.
Response parsing: if response.ok, parse as RainCheckResponse and set answerData. If !response.ok, parse as ErrorResponse and set errorData.
Focus management: after API response (success or error), return focus to input field using inputRef.current?.focus() for easy re-search.
Stateless architecture (ADR-002): No localStorage or sessionStorage. No caching of responses. Fresh data every request.
Performance requirement: Total answer delivery time must be under 2 seconds. Loading state must appear within 100ms of form submission.

ideas.idea: Test valid location search with city name (e.g., "San Francisco") - verify POST request to /api/check-rain with correct headers and body format, verify response displays in AnswerDisplay component
Test valid location search with ZIP code (e.g., "94102") - verify backend handles ZIP codes correctly, verify YES/NO answer displays correctly
Test YES answer scenario - search location with high rain probability (≥50%), verify rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows all display correctly
Test NO answer scenario - search location with low rain probability (<50%), verify probability displays, verify no additional details shown
Test close call scenario - search location with 40-49% probability, verify close call message appears
Test invalid location error - search for "XYZ123" or nonsense location, verify ErrorDisplay shows "invalid_location" error with user-friendly message
Test API failure scenario - simulate 500 error (may require backend modification or mock), verify ErrorDisplay shows "service_unavailable" error
Test network error - disconnect internet or block API route, verify ErrorDisplay shows "network_error" with message "Network connection failed. Please check your internet and try again."
Test multiple sequential searches - search location, get result, search different location, verify previous results are cleared and new results display correctly
Test state reset between searches - verify answerData and errorData are mutually exclusive, verify isLoading resets correctly, verify focus returns to input
Verify TypeScript compilation with npm run type-check - no type errors related to API integration
Verify types match between frontend and backend - inspect types/api.ts interfaces, compare with app/api/check-rain/route.ts response structure
Verify request format in Network tab - Content-Type: application/json header present, request body is {location: string} format
Verify response format in Network tab - successful responses match RainCheckResponse interface, error responses match ErrorResponse interface
